title: Crosslingual cluster interpretability and anchor analysis
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an exploratory evaluation and heuristic playbook for using anchors to interpret and sanity-check cross-lingual embedding clusters. Goal is two-fold: (1) produce a small, repeatable seedset + annotation protocol we can use during model onboarding and regression checks, and (2) codify heuristics for choosing anchors (seed exemplars) that surface subtle failures (translation drift, script effects, high-frequency tokens, domain bleed).

Background & motivation:
- We onboard a lot of embedding variants (different families, quantized builds, sparse/PRF-style transforms).
- Standard metrics (NDCG on retrieval) catch many regressions but miss cluster-level oddities that affect downstream semantic search rerankers and clustering tasks.
- Anchors (human-chosen exemplars) let us ask: does the embedding space keep semantically similar items near each other across languages and domains?

Dataset composition (seedset):
- Languages: English (en), Spanish (es), French (fr), Chinese (zh), Arabic (ar), Hindi (hi), Russian (ru), Portuguese (pt)
- Domains: e-commerce product titles, Wikipedia short intros, consumer health Q&A, legal short clauses (redacted), developer forum titles (StackOverflow-like)
- Per-language/per-domain: 250 canonical items (carefully curated), plus 100 synthetic paraphrases and 50 noisy variants (typos, punctuation, code fragments)
- Total seedset size ~ (8 langs) * (4 domains) * (400) = ~12,800 items (small but representative)

Anchor selection heuristics (how to pick anchors):
1) Frequency-balanced central anchors
   - Pick tokens/phrases that occur across domains but avoid top-of-corpus stopwords.
   - Compute centroid of candidate cluster in embedding space and pick nearest real exemplar.
2) Translation-consistency anchors
   - For an English exemplar, pick its translations (human or high-quality MT) across languages and enforce that pairwise cosine distances remain low and monotonic across model versions.
3) Adversarial anchors
   - Deliberately pick ambiguous phrases ("apple" monthly report vs company) and near-homographs in other scripts to surface disambiguation regressions.
4) Low-resource morphological anchors
   - Select short stems and morphological variants in Hindi/Arabic to check subword/tokenization artifacts.
5) Domain-transfer anchors
   - Items that should cluster by meaning across domains, e.g., product description vs product review snippet.

Interpretability pipeline (steps):
- Step 0: Preprocess consistent tokenization/normalization per language (record exact pipeline used).
- Step 1: Embed the full seedset for model X and model Y (reference). Store embeddings and hash of model config.
- Step 2: For each anchor, compute k-NN (k=20) and record language distribution, domain distribution, and mean distance.
- Step 3: UMAP (n_components=2, random_state=42) visualizations per domain/language and combined, with anchors highlighted.
- Step 4: Cluster (HDBSCAN with min_cluster_size=15) and compute cluster purity by language and domain, plus ARI vs gold labels.
- Step 5: Anchor-consistency metric: for each anchor a, define AC(a)=mean_cos_sim(anchor, translations) - mean_cos_sim(anchor, random-sample-of-same-lang). Track AC percentiles across anchors.

Metrics and regression criteria:
- Retrieval-style: NDCG@10, MRR on language-internal retrieval tasks (already tracked elsewhere).
- Cluster metrics: purity (language and domain), ARI, silhouette_score (cosine-based).
- Anchor-specific: AC (above), translation-distance delta (model_new - model_ref), neighbor-lang-entropy (entropy of language labels in kNN).
- Thresholds (initial proposals):
   * If median AC drops by >0.05 from baseline -> flag regression.
   * If language neighbor-entropy increases by >10% for >25% of anchors -> investigate tokenization or script-level drift.
   * If cluster purity for any domain drops by >7 points -> run targeted human annotation.

Sample experimental run (high-level results, Feb 2025 run):
- Models compared: redwood-embed-v1 (baseline), open-embed-lite-quant (candidate), redwood-embed-v1-8bit (quantized)
- Observations:
   * redwood-embed-v1-8bit: overall NDCG@10 -1.2 pts vs baseline, but cluster purity (avg domain) dropped -3.1 pts; AC median stable (-0.01). Hypothesis: small numeric noise affecting tight clusters but retrieval still acceptable.
   * open-embed-lite-quant: NDCG -2.7 pts, cluster purity -9.5 pts, AC median -0.08. Notably, Arabic/Hindi anchors had much higher neighbor-lang-entropy -> likely tokenization mismatch.
- Quick interpret notes: for open-embed-lite-quant we saw many Hindi short stems push towards a small English-dominated cluster (subword boundary mismatch).

Annotation protocol (human in the loop):
- For any flagged cluster or anchor set: assemble 50 nearest neighbors across languages and present to annotators (4 annotators per item).
- Task: label each neighbor as SAME_CONCEPT / RELATED / UNRELATED. Free-text why if RELATED/UNRELATED.
- Accept if majority SAME_CONCEPT >= 3/4, else mark as failure case.
- Inter-annotator agreement target: Krippendorff alpha >= 0.6; if lower, revise labeling instructions.

Prompt sets for annotators (short):
- Instruction: "You will see a highlighted anchor (with language). For each candidate below, choose whether it represents the same primary concept as the anchor. Ignore surface differences (plural/synonym) unless they change the primary meaning."
- Examples include multi-language exemplars and anti-examples (homographs, translated idioms).

QC heuristics for annotations:
- Insert 10 gold checks per batch (created from high-confidence translation pairs).
- Drop annotator if accuracy on gold < 80% or if time-per-item deviates by >3x median.

Visualization checklist (for PRs):
- UMAP with anchors labeled + kNN ribbons drawn to translations.
- Per-anchor violin plots for neighbor distances (by language).
- Language distribution heatmap for kNNs.
- Mini-report: 3 biggest failure anchors + 3 representative good anchors with explanations.

Common failure modes we've observed (notes):
- Script conflation: Latinized Arabic or Pinyin variants cluster unexpectedly with English because of lexical overlap.
- High-frequency tokens: product model numbers or brand tokens dominate neighbor lists -> need frequency debiasing or stoplist.
- Tokenization drift: quantized models with small vocab changes cause short stems to map differently (esp. morphologically rich languages).
- Domain bleed: e.g., legal boilerplate phrases cluster across languages more than semantically-similar consumer queries.

Actions & TODOs (next experiments):
- (Ethan) Run anchor-consistency sweep at k=5/10/20 for the next model candidate set. Compare %-of-anchors failing at each k. Due 2025-03-10.
- (Priya) Add automatic script-detection step to flag mixed-script anchors and produce separate AC metrics.
- (Marta) Produce a small bilingual glossary (EN-XX) for the ambiguous anchors set and push to Confluence.
- Test: apply frequency-debiasing (subtract top-1000 token centroid) and rerun cluster purity on open-embed-lite-quant.

Open questions / discussion points:
- What is the right operational threshold for AC delta? 0.05 is a guess; need empirical ROC-style tuning using historical regressions.
- Should we weight anchors by domain importance (search vs clustering downstream)? Probably, yes — add priority tiers.
- How to integrate this into CI without exploding annotation costs? Idea: run lightweight automatic checks and only surface items with metric deltas for annotation.

Notes to self (incomplete/fragments):
- Keep anchor list size small (50-200) to be actionable.
- Consider multilingual anchors where one exemplar is a phrase that doesn't translate literally (idioms). Good stress test.
- Remember to log exact model commit hash + tokenization config in artifact metadata.

References / artifacts:
- Confluence anchor playbook (link above)
- GitHub eval harness PR (link above)
- JIRA:ML-1183 tracks open-embed-lite-quant onboarding

Appendix: quick pseudocode for AC metric
- def anchor_consistency(anchor_id, translations, embeddings):
    anchor_vec = embeddings[anchor_id]
    trans_vecs = [embeddings[t] for t in translations]
    pos = mean(cosine(anchor_vec, v) for v in trans_vecs)
    neg = mean(cosine(anchor_vec, random_same_lang_samples))
    return pos - neg

(End of doc)
